summary: The current iteration substantially expands the model (media, risk, retailer, location compliance) and improves modularity, but a syntax error in Simulation.evaluate breaks execution, and several state-mutation and metric issues risk incorrect or duplicated results. Fix the IndentationError, remove duplicated metric assignments, centralize state mutation in Simulation.run (and remove it from AdoptionAggregator), and align evaluation metrics with the task specification (post-policy sustainability, exposure to misinformation, compliance under mandate).

critical_issues.issue: IndentationError in Simulation.evaluate caused by mis-indented metric assignments
critical_issues.impact: Prevents the simulation from running at all; blocks any evaluation and artifact creation
critical_issues.solution: Properly indent the lines assigning metrics["time_to_threshold_70"] and remove the stray one-liner duplication of time_to_50_percent. See code_snippets[0].

critical_issues.issue: Duplicate and premature state mutations in AdoptionAggregator.forward
critical_issues.impact: Double-appends enforcement/compliance histories per day and risks inconsistencies across series; prev_mask_use is set in the aggregator instead of the central commit phase, potentially corrupting churn calculations
critical_issues.solution: Remove AdoptionAggregator updates to state (prev_mask_use, compliance_by_type_history, enforcement_actions_history); update prev_mask_use inside Simulation.run commit when current_mask_use is committed. See code_snippets[1] and [2].

critical_issues.issue: Duplicate assignment of time_to_50_percent metric in Simulation.evaluate
critical_issues.impact: Confusing and error-prone metric computation that can hide bugs and contributes to the syntax issue
critical_issues.solution: Delete the stray next(...) line and keep the single loop-based computation. See code_snippets[0].

critical_issues.issue: Evaluation metrics misaligned with task specification
critical_issues.impact: Missing or inconsistently named metrics (e.g., post_policy_sustainability vs sustained_adoption_after_policy_lift, exposure_to_misinformation not reported, compliance_under_mandate not summarized) reduces the utility of outputs for analysis
critical_issues.solution: Compute and expose the expected metrics: post_policy_sustainability, exposure_to_misinformation, compliance_under_mandate; ensure naming matches the specification. See code_snippets[3].

critical_issues.issue: MAE_cumulative_adopters computed against a None series
critical_issues.impact: Produces misleading or undefined comparisons; can confuse calibration/evaluation
critical_issues.solution: Set MAE_cumulative_adopters to NaN when no simulator cumulative time series exists or compute a proper cumulative-by-day series; as a quick fix, set to NaN. See code_snippets[3].

model_improvements.current_approach: Only daily compliance_by_type and daily compliance_under_mandate (None when inactive) exist; evaluation does not summarize compliance under mandate vs not
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Aggregate compliance under mandate (average adoption rate during mandate days) and report separately from non-mandate periods; also compute the requested compliance_under_mandate metric
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Clearer interpretability of policy effects and alignment with evaluation metrics

model_improvements.current_approach: MediaBroadcast computes daily misinformation rate but evaluation does not summarize it
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Compute exposure_to_misinformation as mean daily rate across full period and, optionally, by phase (pre/during/post mandate)
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Improved tracking of media environments and better alignment with evaluation metrics

model_improvements.current_approach: Computed as sustained_adoption_after_policy_lift but with a non-standard name and limited window handling
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Rename to post_policy_sustainability, ensure window bounds are valid, and fallback gracefully if series is short
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Alignment with metric spec and robust computation on short runs

model_improvements.current_approach: Only a single final cumulative count is tracked; MAE computed vs ground truth using a placeholder None series
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Track cumulative unique adopters by day (already possible using ever_adopted in aggregator) and compute MAE only if such series is available; otherwise return NaN
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Meaningful comparison to real data when provided; avoids misleading metrics

model_improvements.current_approach: Poisson household sizes are created but overwritten by a round-robin assignment; household size distribution is not actually used
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Either: (a) actually assign members according to sampled sizes; or (b) simplify and remove unused household size logic to avoid confusion
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Cleaner model logic and potential to use household norms realistically later

code_improvements.modification: Fix mis-indentation in Simulation.evaluate and remove duplicate time_to_50_percent next(...) assignment
code_improvements.reason: Resolves a syntax error blocking execution and avoids redundant computations

code_improvements.modification: Stop AdoptionAggregator from mutating global state (prev_mask_use, compliance/enforcement histories)
code_improvements.reason: Keeps state updates centralized, prevents double-counting, and stabilizes churn computation

code_improvements.modification: Update prev_mask_use in Simulation.run when committing current_mask_use_today
code_improvements.reason: Ensures churn calculation in subsequent steps has a correct baseline without relying on aggregator

code_improvements.modification: Align evaluation metric names and add missing metrics: post_policy_sustainability (rename), exposure_to_misinformation (average), and compliance_under_mandate (average during mandate days)
code_improvements.reason: Aligns with the task specification and makes outputs more actionable

code_improvements.modification: Set MAE_cumulative_adopters to NaN if no time series; remove placeholder comparison against None
code_improvements.reason: Avoids misleading metrics and potential downstream confusion

code_improvements.modification: Optionally remove unused variables like chan_count; keep modules side-effect free
code_improvements.reason: Cleaner code and reduced confusion; minor but helpful for maintenance

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Metric is computed under a different name and may not handle short series well
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Compute metrics["post_policy_sustainability"] as average adoption in [mandate_end_day+1, +30], guard for available length, and name exactly as specified

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Daily rate exists but no summary metric is reported
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Compute metrics["exposure_to_misinformation"] = mean(misinformation_rate_history) over the simulation period

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: No explicit top-level metric summarizing mandate compliance
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: During evaluation, average adoption rates across days where policy was active; report as metrics["compliance_under_mandate"]

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Reported as inequality_index_by_group but not named per spec
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Set metrics["group_adoption_disparity"] = inequality_index_by_group to match the expected naming

prioritized_actions: Fix IndentationError and duplicate time_to_50_percent assignment in Simulation.evaluate
Remove state mutations from AdoptionAggregator (prev_mask_use, compliance/enforcement histories) and set prev_mask_use in Simulation.run commit
Add/rename evaluation metrics to match specification: post_policy_sustainability, exposure_to_misinformation, compliance_under_mandate, and group_adoption_disparity
Set MAE_cumulative_adopters to NaN unless a simulator cumulative-by-day series is available
Optional: Clean up unused variables (e.g., chan_count) and clarify household assignment logic
additional_comments: Do not add a standard if __name__ == "__main__" guard; the system requires a direct main() call at the end. The early stopping environment override is correctly set in evaluate_params; consider restoring the previous value afterward for cleanliness, but it's not critical. NetworkX and Matplotlib are handled robustly. The module dependency order is sound. After fixes, run a quick py_compile check to ensure no remaining indentation or syntax issues remain.

change_analysis.summary: This iteration greatly enhances the simulation scope and modularity (network formation rewiring, communication decay, media/misinformation, risk signal, policy enforcement with mask requirements, retailer stock/purchases, location-level compliance, and improved aggregation). However, a copy/paste error introduced a syntax-breaking indentation issue, and aggregator-level state mutations now conflict with the centralized commit logic, causing duplicated histories and potential churn miscalculation.
positive_impacts: Added MediaBroadcast and RiskSignal integrates key drivers (media stance, perceived risk) into adoption decisions
Retailer and stock dynamics introduce resource constraints, making desired vs observed behavior more realistic
LocationCompliance with enforcement bridges policy to actual observed compliance at work/public
Parameter registry and pluggable calibration architecture improved
Stronger robustness in file handling, seeding, and modular I/O persistence
negative_impacts: IndentationError in Simulation.evaluate prevents any run
AdoptionAggregator mutates global state creating double-counted histories and fragile churn baseline
Duplicated metric assignment and naming inconsistencies reduce clarity
Household sizing logic not actually used to control distribution
suggestions: Fix syntax and duplicated metric assignments immediately
Keep all state mutations in Simulation.run commit; modules should only read inputs and write to buffers
Align metric names and add missing aggregate metrics to match the task specification
Optionally rationalize household assignment (or remove unused complexity) to avoid confusion
